title: Plan migrations with the Cloud Adoption Framework
learningObjective: Evaluate a migration approach that uses the Cloud Adoption Framework, and evaluate on-premises servers, data and applications for migration.
foundation: Big migrations fail when they start with servers instead of goals. The Cloud Adoption Framework (CAF) is Microsoft's step-by-step method.
First agree why you are moving, then plan which apps go where, prepare a landing zone, and only then move workloads in waves.
Azure Migrate discovers what you have, measures how it performs, maps dependencies and estimates Azure cost.
engineer: CAF methodologies: Strategy (motivations, business outcomes, business case), Plan (digital estate inventory and rationalisation, skills, adoption plan), Ready (Azure landing zones: identity, network topology, governance, management, security), Adopt (Migrate and Modernize/Innovate), plus Govern, Secure and Manage across the lifecycle. Migration waves group workloads by dependency and risk; start with low-risk workloads.
Rationalisation (the Rs): retire, retain, rehost (lift and shift), replatform (minimal changes to use PaaS), refactor (code changes for cloud-native), rearchitect, rebuild, replace with SaaS.

Assessment with Azure Migrate: agentless discovery of VMware, Hyper-V and physical servers through the Azure Migrate appliance (or CSV import), performance-based right-sizing, Azure readiness, cost estimates, business case (TCO comparison), dependency analysis (agentless or agent-based) to group servers that must move together, and assessments for SQL Server, web apps and AVS. Database assessments flag compatibility issues for SQL Database, Managed Instance or SQL on VMs.

animation.caption: Place activities in CAF phases and choose Azure Migrate for discovery and assessment.

example.title: Exiting a datacenter in 18 months
body: Strategy: leadership agrees to exit the datacenter lease and cut run costs by 20%. Plan: Azure Migrate discovers 600 servers; dependency analysis groups them into 12 waves; each app gets a decision (rehost, replatform, replace, retire).
Ready: the landing zone (management groups, hub network, policies) is deployed with Bicep before the first wave. Adopt: wave 1 rehosts low-risk internal apps.

prerequisites: An Azure subscription; most design reviews need only Reader access
permissions: Reader to review existing resources; Contributor or Owner to build the design
limits: Check service limits and regional availability for each component
portal: Azure Migrate > Servers, databases and web apps > Discover: download the appliance or import a CSV.
Azure Migrate > Assess: Azure VM, Azure SQL, web apps, AVS; Business case.

troubleshooting.symptom: Migrated app breaks because a dependent server was left on-premises.
troubleshooting.fix: Run dependency analysis and move dependent servers in the same wave.

troubleshooting.symptom: Azure cost is much higher than expected after rehosting.

comparisons.difference: Rehost moves as-is to VMs; replatform makes small changes to use PaaS such as App Service or SQL MI.
Ready prepares the landing zone; Adopt moves the workloads.

misconceptions.reality: It starts with strategy, planning and a landing zone.
Performance-based sizing usually recommends smaller Azure sizes.

architectureDecisions: Follow CAF: strategy, plan, ready, adopt.
Discover and assess with Azure Migrate, using performance data and dependency analysis.
Move in waves, low risk first.

walkthrough.subtitle: Move to Azure in a planned, low-risk way: goals first, then plan, prepare, and move in waves.
learn: Discover and assess with Azure Migrate

steps.label: Problem
steps.title: 600 servers and a lease ending
body: Moving everything at once is risky and moving nothing is expensive. You need a method.

steps.label: CAF
steps.title: Four steps before and during the move
body: Strategy: why move? Plan: inventory and decide per app. Ready: build the landing zone. Adopt: migrate and modernise. Govern, Secure and Manage run throughout.

steps.label: Rationalise
steps.title: A decision for every app
body: Retire what nobody uses, retain what must stay, rehost to move fast, replatform to use PaaS with small changes, refactor or rebuild for cloud-native, or replace with SaaS.

steps.label: Assess
steps.title: Azure Migrate does the counting
body: An agentless appliance discovers servers and collects performance data. Assessments recommend Azure sizes and costs; dependency analysis shows which servers talk to each other, so they move in the same wave.

steps.label: Recap
steps.title: Migration planning
recap: Strategy → Plan → Ready → Adopt (+ Govern, Secure, Manage)
Retire, retain, rehost, replatform, refactor, replace
Azure Migrate: discovery, performance sizing, dependencies, business case

handsOn.title: Assess servers with Azure Migrate (CSV import)
handsOn.cost: Free. Azure Migrate discovery and assessment are free; this lab imports a CSV instead of deploying an appliance.
before: Signed in at portal.azure.com as Owner of a subscription. Work in a resource group called rg-az305-lab.
If rg-az305-lab does not exist yet: Resource groups > Create > name rg-az305-lab, region UAE North (or any region near you) > Review + create > Create.

steps.do: Search 'Azure Migrate' > Servers, databases and web apps > Create project: rg-az305-lab, project name migrate-lab, a geography near you.
Discover > Import using CSV > Download the template.
steps.see: A CSV template with columns such as server name, cores, memory, OS and disks.

steps.do: Fill in three rows, for example: web01 (2 cores, 8 GB, Windows Server 2019), app01 (4 cores, 16 GB), db01 (8 cores, 64 GB). Save and upload.
steps.see: Import succeeds; three servers appear in the inventory after a few minutes.

steps.do: Assess > Azure VM: sizing criteria As on-premises (CSV has no performance data); target region near you. Group: create a group with the three servers. Create assessment.

steps.see: Azure readiness, recommended VM sizes and monthly cost estimates.
steps.tip: With the real appliance, performance-based sizing usually recommends smaller, cheaper sizes.

steps.do: Look at the Business case option (don't build it).
steps.see: On-premises vs Azure cost comparison over time.

check: The assessment shows readiness and a cost estimate for three servers.
cleanup: Delete the Azure Migrate project (or the resource group).
Resource groups > rg-az305-lab > Delete resource group > type the name > Delete.
